purpose: Wall time of the perturbation workflow (conditional randomization test) on panels of the Gasperini screen, with RapidGLM's defaults and with fit_check ks
commit_note: Library code of v1.4.0-dev.4; all final release measurements were run on this commit.
configuration: 207,324 cells, moi high, complement controls, CRT, budgets 499/4,999/19,999, screen 0.02, cell_qc false, seed 20260930, 16 threads on CPUs 16-31; default: fit_check strict with 199,999 confirmation draws; ks: fit_check ks
panels: every pair of T targets and G response genes: the first T of a random order of the benchmark panel's 3,776 discovery targets and the first G of a random order of its 7,418 response genes (numpy default_rng(20261001): one permutation of the sorted target names, then one of the gene indices), so the sets are nested; written by scripts/prepare_crt_panels.py
host: One workstation: Intel Core i9-13900KF, 125 GiB RAM; BIOS 1836, microcode 0x133, 253 W sustained and short-term limits; 4 x 32 GiB at 4,200 MT/s. Turbo is on. Two faulty performance cores (logical CPUs 8-11) are capped at 2.2 GHz and never used for timing. Every timed run is pinned to the 16 identical efficiency cores, one thread per core, under the shared lock after a quiet-host check. Pinning to identical cores makes the comparisons reproducible. The efficiency cores retain their stock 800 MHz-4.3 GHz range. Absolute seconds from other host settings are not directly comparable; use matched speed-up ratios across settings. These timings are final, not provisional. Final timings on the 16 identical efficiency cores (CPUs 16-31), one thread per core: one on 16, four on 16-19, eight on 16-23, twelve on 16-27, sixteen on 16-31. Each timed command holds the shared lock and starts after two consecutive ten-second quiet samples: one-minute load <=4 and every selected CPU <20% busy. Both samples are retained. Untimed work uses CPUs 0-7 under nice 10. These release timings are final, not provisional.
